title.narrative: Integrated multi-sector assistance to support conflict-affected population in Gobu Sayo woreda, East Wollega Zone, Oromia Region (Priority 2)

description.narrative: ltpgtFIDO and Swiss Church Aid (HEKS/EPER), are proposing an integrated multi-sector assistance to support vulnerable communities in conflict affected areas in Gobu Sayo Woreda, East Wollega zone, Oromia Region.ltbrgtProtracted conflict has left populations in this woreda isolated and vulnerable, with approximately 948 households live in rented homes in Ano Town, facing eviction risks due to inability to pay rent. Overcrowding, inadequate WASH facilities, and lack of health and nutrition services increase exposure to GBV and communicable diseases. A recent needs assessment identified Health, Nutrition, Emergency shelter/NFIs, WASH, and Agriculture as priority sectors. FIDO will lead in Health, Nutrition, and Emergency shelter/NFIs, while HEKS/EPER will lead in WASH and Agriculture, collaborating to address community needs comprehensively amidst inter-ethnic and political conflict.ltbrgtltbrgtIn the agriculture sector, the project aims to support 700 HH by providing agricultural inputs and tools. In addition, 120 families will be supported with voucher-based support for livestock treatment. Four veterinary health facilities, will receive necessary medications, and two vaccination campaigns will be organized to ensure the health and wellbeing of the livestock population.ltbrgtThe Nutrition and Health Sector aims to support vulnerable populations, focusing on infants, young children, and pregnant/lactating women. Through nutrition screening and interventions, mental health support, and strengthening health systems, it targets 4748 children under 5 and 1919 pregnant/lactating women. Additionally, it plans to enhance health facilities and extend services to hard-to-reach areas through Mental Health and Nutrition Team (MHNT) and collaboration with Health Extension Workers (HEWs). The Health Sector targets essential health service delivery for 25,709 individuals, including OPD consultations, ANC/PNC, skilled deliveries, and immunization campaigns. It also aims to rehabilitate damaged health center and conduct community engagement activities alongside risk communication.ltbrgtUnder the WASH, the project seeks to improve access to safe water and sanitation facilities for 8,480 persons. Rehabilitation of water schemes through the replacement of pumps in 2 shallow wells, will be carried out. Additionally, life-saving WASH Non-Food Items (NFIs) will be distributed for 850 HH to further enhance hygiene practices and reduce the risk of disease outbreaks.ltbrgtUnder emergency Shelter, cash for rental support to 821 HH conflict affected IDPs living in Gobu Soyu Woreda per the cluster recommendation.ltbrgtFurthermore, training, together with HEKS/EPER will be provided to communities, government staff and project committees on AAP, PSEAH and GBV. Joint monitoring and PDM will be conducted. The project was designed in consultation with relevant UN Clusters and due attention was given to complementarity with other projects funded by CERF/CBPF. ltbrgtThe consortium has secured 15,000 USD in core funding from internal sources to supplement the requested funding, acknowledging the significant needs in the target woredas. By pooling resources and coordinating efforts across sectors, the project aims to tackle the complex challenges faced by conflict-affected communities, providing immediate lifesaving assistance and fostering resilience and sustainable recovery in Gobu Soyu.ltbrgtlt/pgt
